## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical gate design for multi-tenant environments with real tooling and secrets handling.

## Key Concepts
- Cosign signature verification against a repository public key
- Digest pinning and non-latest image references in manifests/Helm
- External secrets management (Vault, CSI or AppRole) with projected secrets
- RBAC + admission controls to prevent plaintext secrets
- Local and CI validation workflows

## Code Example
```yaml
name: gate-ci
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize]
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Setup cosign
        run: |
          cosign version
          cosign verify -key cosign.pub registry.example.com/namespace/service@digest
      - name: Lint manifests & charts
        run: |
          helm lint charts/
          yq eval '(.spec.template.spec.containers[].image) != ""' manifests/**/*.yaml
      - name: Validate Vault refs
        run: |
          echo "Vault refs resolved and projected secrets configured" 
```

- How would you detect drift between SBOMs and deployed images at runtime?

```yaml
# .github/workflows/netpol-gate.yml
name: NetPol Gate
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  netpol-check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: azure/setup-kubectl@v3
        with:
          version: 'latest'
      - run: kubectl version --client
      - run: |
          for ns in $(kubectl get ns -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'); do

          done
```

```

```yaml

apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: default-deny
  namespace: default

  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes: [Ingress, Egress]
  ingress: []
  egress: []

name: prod-provenance
on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - manifests/prod/**
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: setup cosign
        run: |
          curl -sSfL https://github.com/sigstore/cosign/releases/download/v1.10.0/cosign-linux-amd64 -o cosign

          sudo mv cosign /usr/local/bin/

          cosign verify -key cosign.pub registry.example.com/namespace/service:tag
      - name: verify SBOM attestation
        run: |
          cyclone_dx_attest --image registry.example.com/namespace/service:tag --attest
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Fintech workloads handling sensitive financial data demand strict data-protection posture. This question validates your understanding of end-to-end security enforcement—from CI gates that catch misconfigurations before deployment to runtime policies that protect running workloads.

## Key Concepts
- CI gate for manifest validation at pull request stage
- Resource requests/limits for resource governance
- readOnlyRootFilesystem for filesystem security
- TLS secret mounting with tls-cert-<app> naming convention
- Runtime policy enforcement via Kyverno or OPA
- Verification strategies for both CI and cluster runtime

## Code Example
```yaml
# Kyverno ClusterPolicy
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-secure-deploy
spec:
  rules:
  - name: enforce-resources-readonly
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Deployment
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "Deployment must set resources.limits, resources.requests, and readOnlyRootFilesystem: true"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              securityContext:
                readOnlyRootFilesystem: "true"
              containers:
              - resources:
                  limits:
                    memory: "?*"
                    cpu: "?*"
                  requests:
                    memory: "?*"
                    cpu: "?*"
  - name: enforce-tls-secret-mount
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "TLS secret must be mounted at /etc/tls from Secret tls-cert-<app>"
      pattern:
        spec:
          volumes:
          - secret:
              secretName: tls-cert-?*
              items:
              - key: tls.crt
                path: etc/tls/tls.crt
```

## Sample Compliant Manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: tls-cert-payment-service
type: kubernetes.io/tls
data:
  tls.crt: <base64-cert>
  tls.key: <base64-key>
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: payment-service
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    spec:
      securityContext:
        readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: payment-service:latest
        resources:
          limits:
            memory: "512Mi"
            cpu: "500m"
          requests:
            memory: "256Mi"
            cpu: "250m"
        volumeMounts:
        - name: tls-certs
          mountPath: /etc/tls
          readOnly: true
      volumes:
      - name: tls-certs
        secret:
          secretName: tls-cert-payment-service
```

## Sample Non-Compliant Manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: insecure-service
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: insecure-service:latest
        # Missing: resources.limits/requests
        # Missing: readOnlyRootFilesystem
        # Missing: TLS secret mount
```

## GitHub Actions CI Gate
```yaml
name: Security Gate
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  security-check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    - name: Install kubeval
      run: |4
        curl -L -o kubeval https://github.com/instrumenta/kubeval/releases/latest/download/kubeval-linux-amd64.tar.gz
        tar xf kubeval-linux-amd64.tar.gz
        sudo mv kubeval /usr/local/bin
    - name: Validate manifests
      run: |
        for f in k8s/*.yaml; do
          kubeval --strict --additional-schema-locations=https://kubernetesjsonschema.dev $f || exit 1
        done
    - name: Check resource limits
      run: |
        yq -e '.spec.template.spec.containers[].resources.limits' k8s/*.yaml || exit 1
    - name: Check readOnlyRootFilesystem
      run: |
        yq -e '.spec.template.spec.securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem == true' k8s/*.yaml || exit 1
    - name: Check TLS secret mounting
      run: |
        yq -e '.spec.template.spec.volumes[].secret.secretName | test("^tls-cert-")' k8s/*.yaml || exit 1
```

## Verification Steps

### CI Verification
1. Create a PR with the non-compliant manifest—pipeline should fail
2. Update to compliant manifest—pipeline should pass
3. Confirm all three checks (resources, readOnlyRootFilesystem, TLS) are enforced

### Runtime Verification
1. Apply Kyverno policy to test cluster
2. Attempt to deploy non-compliant manifest—deployment should be blocked
3. Verify policy logs show rejection reason
4. Apply compliant manifest—deployment should succeed

## Code Example
```javascript
# Minimal Kyverno policy (YAML shown as JS block for readability)
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: Policy
metadata:
  name: enforce-basic-security
spec:
  rules:
  - name: require-psp
    match:
      any:
        - resources:
            kinds: [Namespace, Pod]
    mutate:

        {"spec": {"securityContext": {"readOnlyRootFilesystem": true, "allowPrivilegeEscalation": false}}}
```

# Failing manifest (privileged container)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: bad-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox
    securityContext:
      privileged: true
```
```javascript
# Passing manifest (no privileged, readOnlyRootFilesystem)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: good-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app

      readOnlyRootFilesystem: true

## Code Example
```yaml

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: feature-service
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: feature-service
        data_version: v1.2.3

```yaml
# minimal GitHub Actions snippet (validation)
name: Validate Provenance
on: [push]
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Inspect image for digest and labels
        run: |
          CONTAINER_IMG='registry.example.com/feature-service@sha256:abcdef...'
          DIGEST=$(docker inspect --format='{{index .RepoDigests 0}}' $CONTAINER_IMG | cut -d'@' -f2)
          LABELS=$(docker inspect --format='{{.Config.Labels}}' $CONTAINER_IMG)
          if [[ -z "$DIGEST" || "$LABELS" != *data_version* || "$LABELS" != *model_version* ]]; then
            exit 1
          fi
      - name: Canary trace test
        run: |
          # pseudo-step: send request and verify OTLP trace propagates
          curl -sS http://feature-service.canary/health -H 'traceparent: 00-abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789-1234567812345678-01' >/dev/null
          # verification would query OTLP collector for trace-id
          echo 'Canary test passed'
```

## Follow-up Questions
